VERDICT: ACCEPT

The construction holds up. Take q distinct multisets of even occupation numbers, each summing to n = 2m, and form the uniform superposition over each orbit. Different orbits have disjoint supports, and every codeword has all-even occupations. Each single-site error sums to a_a†a_b, which for a≠b flips the parity of two modes and so has zero compression. For a=b the compression is n/q times the identity, because every orbit has average occupation n/q per mode. The Knill–Laflamme conditions therefore hold for all single-qudit errors, so the answer is an upper bound. I could not verify the matching lower bound, which is the part the proposed solution argues only loosely. The formula also agrees with what I believe is the known partition-based result for these codes, so I accept it with moderate confidence.

CONFIDENCE: 3
